title: Annotatio V §.XI: Author §.XIX cover — Subject error substitutes Calvin alone for Reformed
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless the Vindication by which the Author tries to veil this elenchus aberration of his in §. XIX is of the same, indeed a worse, stamp, piling one on two others, when he tries to confirm that the Reformed have seceded from Irenaeus’s mind and words, of which one wanders from the Subject of the Question, the other from the Predicate: He wanders from the Subject when he substitutes Calvin alone in place of the Reformed — as if Reformed and Calvin were synonymous names or convertible terms.
pass_b_english: His §.XIX vindication only worsens the miss: he piles new slips while claiming the Reformed left Irenaeus’s mind and words.
Subject error: he swaps Calvin alone for “the Reformed,” as if Reformed and Calvin were one name.
source_text: Nihilominus Vindicatio, quâ Autor hanc Elenchi aberrationem suam obvelare studet §. XIX, ejusdem, imô deterioris, commatis est, unam duabus aliis cumulans, quando Reformatos ab Irenæi mente & verbis secessisse confirmare conatur, quarum una à Subjectô Quæstionis, altera à Prædicato deviat: A Subjecto aberrat, dum Reformatorum in locum, unicum Calvinum substituit; quasi verò Reformati & Calvinus nomina essent Synonyma, vel termini convertibiles.

lemmas.gloss: from the Subject of the Question
